messages:
sanjay: quick heads-up — noticed a host-side latency regression correlated with the kernel-selector rollout last night. p50 went ~12ms -> ~28ms, p95 ~120ms -> ~360ms. KV cache hit rate for small requests dropped from ~87% to ~63%. looks like small-batch traffic is getting punished. :eyes:
perfbot: automated profile (snapshot 5971230000) attached: top stacks by CPU%: host::parse::tokenize 35%, kernel_selector::choose 22%, kv_cache::fetch 18%, grpc::writev 5%. full flamegraph: internal link (perf/graphs/5971230000).
maria: can you paste the flamegraph ascii or the hot stacks? afraid the link won't open for everyone in a channel.
todd: flame snippet + collection command below. short stacks only (trimmed):
```
# collect command used
./perf/collect --since=5971200000 --until=5971230000 --stacks=100000 --output=5971230000.folded
# top folded stacks (percentages approximate)
host::ingress::parse;host::tokenize 35.1%
host::rpc::dispatch;kernel_selector::choose 22.3%
kv_cache::lookup;kv_cache::miss_handler 18.4%
grpc::writev 5.2%
```
alyssa: my read: kernel-selector change (short-seq priority) seems to bias toward v2 low-latency kernels when seq_len<=8. that reduced GPU decode time for some flows but altered request batching (more single-request batches) and reduced prefix reuse -> kvcache misses. also streaming fragmentation increased writev call counts.
sanjay: rollout details: kernel-selector flags toggled: enable_short_seq=true, pick_v2_priority=0.8 around 02:10 UTC. batching heuristics unchanged in code, but scheduler sees different sequence-length distribution so observed batch sizes shrink. combined effect = higher host CPU and more kv lookups per token.
todd: captured a couple of host logs showing kv churn and per-request overhead:
```
[5971230123.112] [kv] lookup key=<sha1:...> hit=false cost_us=210
[5971230123.113] [host.tokenize] token_count=6 parse_us=420
[5971230123.114] [grpc] writev calls=3 bytes=512 latency_us=180
```
maria: grpc writev fragmentation: noticed average per-request overhead ~+180us on streaming paths for small frames — likely from more small writes vs coalesced buffer. that explains the small constant bump on p50 too.
alyssa: mitigation options: (1) revert kernel-selector short-seq preference, (2) increase batching wait threshold for short-seq path by ~3ms to allow batching to assemble, (3) add small-request prefix caching tuning to avoid miss storm. prefer quick canary rollback + follow-up patch.
sanjay: agreed. I'm going to start a 5% canary rollback of the selector change (kernel-selector.version=legacy) and concurrently patch the batching wait. will watch p95 and kvcache. :thumbsup:
deploybot: deploybot: canary rollout initiated at 5971234500 — kernel-selector.version=legacy -> 5% of hosts. monitoring window 30m, will step to 25% if no regressions.
maria: also create a synthetic microbenchmark that sends 1-4 token requests at QPS similar to production to validate kvcache hit behavior before re-rolling. i'll draft the harness.
todd: opened PR with batching wait tweak for short-seq path (increase wait from 0ms -> 3ms) — PR #3124. will add microbench results.
alyssa: if rollback fixes latency and restores kv hit rate, we should re-evaluate kernel-selection heuristics offline and add a traffic-shape-aware guard so selector doesn't change batchability.
sanjay: plan: 1) monitor canary for 45m, 2) run microbench with current and patched batching heuristics, 3) if canary improves p95 by >40% and kvcache >80% -> promote rollback; else revert rollback and land batching patch behind feature-flag.
maria: FYI metrics to track: p50/p95 host-side parse time, kernel choose CPU%, kv-cache hitrate by seq_len cohort, writev calls per request, small-batch fraction (<4 reqs).
todd: will attach perf snapshots every 10m to the ticket.
sanjay: thanks all — immediate focus: get canary health and microbench data. post updates here. :rocket:
